Danbyte 0.17.0: service level agreements, a new topology Diagram with exports, racks in 2D and 3D with live ports, DIN-rail cabinets, MAC tracking on switch ports, link speeds and capacity on the maps, and upgrades that check and roll back themselves.

> [!NOTE]
> **Upgrading from 0.16.x.** The safest path is re-running the 0.17 installer from the bundle (`sudo tar xzf …`, then `sudo ./install.sh`): it runs the new upgrade stage in full - backup, services stopped, database snapshot, migrations, checks, start, or everything put back. An upgrade started from 0.16's Updates page is still run by 0.16's upgrader; 0.17's `migrate` stops the services first and migrates in one transaction. After an upgrade from the app, Settings → Updates shows one card, **Run this release's root steps**: run `sudo ./install.sh --host-only` from this release's bundle to apply nginx, logrotate and the certificate unit. The upgrade guide (Getting started → Upgrading) has the details.

### Upgrading

- **Each release runs its own upgrade.** The in-app upgrade, an uploaded bundle, automatic updates, `danbyte-admin upgrade` and a re-run of `install.sh` all hand over to the target release's upgrade stage, run as the service user's `danbyte-upgrade.service`. A fix to the upgrade now reaches the upgrade to that release.
- #278 #281 #301 - **Services stop before anything changes, and a failed upgrade rolls back, database included.** Timers, workers, the fast lane, web, websockets, frontend and docs stop before the new code goes in, and start again only once the new release has migrated and `/api/health/`, the admin page and the units pass. Migrations run in one transaction where they can, after a database snapshot only the service account can read; a failure before users are let back in puts back the code, virtualenv, frontend, static files, `.env`, unit links and, when the migration ran, the database. An upgrade with nothing to migrate rolls back only the code, and a migration that loses its database to a restart runs once more. The frontend build and dependency download happen before the downtime.
- **A killed upgrade recovers.** A reboot or kill mid-upgrade is finished or rolled back by a recovery unit before any Danbyte service starts; `danbyte-admin upgrade recover` runs it by hand. The upgrade waits up to 20 minutes for the system's own package updates before it stops anything, and `install.sh` waits for the package lock.
- **Settings → Updates** gains a **Last upgrade** card saying how the last upgrade ended; an automatic or failed upgrade is mailed to the digest recipients and listed on the Jobs page.
- **Automatic updates** pick the newest release, move from one pre-release to the next on the *Any* channel, retry a failure that happened before any service stopped after 1, 4 and 12 hours, and refuse to migrate unattended when the database could not be rolled back.
- #287 - **Root steps run only files root owns.** Re-running the installer upgrades through the same stage, as a unit that survives a dropped SSH session, then runs nginx, logrotate and the certificate unit as the root unit `danbyte-install-host.service`, from a root-only copy of the bundle. `install.sh --host-only` runs those steps alone, `--adopt` replaces a hand-edited nginx site (otherwise the new render lands beside it as `danbyte.conf.new`). The `.env` is written as the service user. 0.16's advice to run `sudo make install-tls-unit` or `host-sync` from the app directory is replaced by the bundle; unpack it with `sudo tar xzf`.
- A re-rendered nginx site keeps its mode, owner, live certificate paths and name, and the installer no longer copies the bundle's self-signed certificate over the one in use. `make host-sync` on a `--no-nginx` install adds no nginx site.
- **A downgrade is refused however the upgrade starts.** `install.sh` now orders releases as the app does (a pre-release is older than its final), and `--force` no longer overrides it.
- An upgrade through `install.sh` ends with what it did - from and to, the root steps, warnings - instead of the fresh install's admin password.
- Every upgrade runs `bootstrap` (new seeds, never a superuser) and `collectstatic`, and disables a `danbyte-backend` or `danbyte-frontend` dev server left running beside `danbyte-web`. On a bundle install the frontend runs on the bundle's own Node (`vendor/node`).
- **Docker:** build, stop the scheduler, workers, fast lane and websockets, then `up -d`, so the old processes are not running while the backend migrates. The container's scheduler runs the new timers.
- **Off 0.16 from the app:** 0.17's `migrate` stops the timers, workers and web, migrates in one transaction and leaves the restart to a unit that waits for 0.16's upgrader to exit. After a migration rolled back in full it removes the files 0.17 added, so the next attempt starts clean; a failed release is not retried every 20 minutes. Timers that fire between the old checkout and the migrate log harmless `column ... does not exist` errors, and a git install upgraded from the Updates page is down for the frontend build too.
- #272 - **Access grants are rewritten** (`auth_api.0024`-`0026`). Users, Groups and Permissions are named on the all-object grants that were administrator grants and taken off every other, including the built-in Operator and Read-only grants; the migration prints what it trimmed. If that would leave nobody able to manage users, those accounts get a grant of their own, *Kept user management (0.17 upgrade)*, split per account, and Settings → Updates lists it until your administrators are in the Administrator group.
- Migrations apply automatically: VLAN status, Wi-Fi security, card lines, natural ordering, IP exclusion and reset, IP defaults, topology photo size, cabinets and DIN rails, tunnel capacity, virtual interface types, uplinks and folded search text (`api.0178`-`0195`), access (`auth_api.0024`-`0026`), dashboards, card lines, the default topology view and port counting (`core.0055`-`0058`), rollups, SLAs, SNMP samples and MAC tracking (`monitoring.0094`-`0108`), and routing on VMs (`routing.0013`). `api.0185` stores addresses saved with a mask bare, and logs a row whose bare address is already taken.
- `danbyte-rollups` (every 5 minutes), `danbyte-sla` (every 15 minutes) and `danbyte-sla-burn` (every minute) are new timers; the upgrade links and enables them. `MONITORING_ROLLUP_HOURLY_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 30) sets how long hourly rollups are kept.
- Rollups record from the upgrade on; `manage.py rollup_checks --backfill 90` builds them from the history already on disk.
- Outposts: MAC tracking with VLANs and per-VLAN tables needs **danbyte-outpost 0.9.0**; older agents keep working the old way.
- #244 - Rendered configs may reorder once: component lists now come in natural order.
- Existing VLANs start without a status; existing SSIDs keep WPA Personal, WPA Enterprise and WEP as legacy modes, with PMF blank.
- A topology view last shown on Wiring or Flat opens on the Diagram and brings its arrangement and zones across, waiting for Save; Wiring's cables become Elbow, Flat's Bendy, and old `?tab=wiring` and `?tab=flat` links open Detailed or Simple.
- Plugins: list pages get the new columns from the plugin's list serializer; mark getters only a detail page needs with `@detail_only`.

### Security

- **Operator and Read-only no longer reach users, groups and permissions.** *All object types* included them, so an Operator could edit groups and grants to give itself more, and Read-only could read every account. It now covers every type but those three; a grant reaches them only by naming them. Holding *change* on Users is what opens the Admin pages and tenant settings, and permissions can no longer be staged or applied through a planned change.
- **People pickers without user administration.** Notification subscriptions, script sharing, viewer invites, task assignees and user or group custom fields list the tenant's people and groups, without email addresses unless you may view users. Script sharing accepts only the script's tenant.
- **Export and label templates stay inside the tenant.** A relation hands a template only this tenant's rows the user may view, and accounts, groups and grants can no longer be a template's subject. Templates that filtered or ordered through a relation, called `values`/`values_list`, or printed an owner's email or groups now render nothing or fail with a security error.
- **Sign-in mail** (invites, password resets, emailed codes) for superusers, deployment admins and people in several tenants goes through the deployment's mail server, not a tenant's relay. Set up deployment email to keep them out of tenant relays.
- #279 - **A site certificate upload could replace another site's certificate** on a shared nginx. The apply unit and `danbyte-admin tls` read only Danbyte's own site and leave a certificate tool's links (certbot's `live/`) alone; the unit runs a root-owned copy of its script in `/usr/local/libexec/danbyte/` and answers in `/var/lib/danbyte-tls/`.
- The installer runs nothing from the app directory as root, release bundles are packed with root as the owner, and restarting services or applying plugins is refused while an upgrade holds the units.
- #255 - Device and VM config renders and config bundles run with the requesting user's permissions.
- #256 - CSV and XLSX exports, the label sheet and SLA reports write a cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a return as text; a CSV import reads it back unchanged.
- **An import could reference another tenant's ports.** MAC address rows and port or VM interface references now resolve through their parent inside the active tenant.
- #293 #295 - An Outpost writes SNMP results only for the devices it polls, checked against the devices it posted; a body that is not an object is a 400.
- #268 #294 - Dashboard monitoring widgets stay empty without IP view, and a photo marker for a port you cannot view stays unresolved, in `GET /api/devices/face-ports/` too.
- Custom-field object labels, compliance's affected rows, a virtual network's VMs, the MAC registry and interface and tunnel IP lists show only what the caller may view.
- #291 - Uploaded photos and image attachments lose their metadata - GPS position, camera and serial, XMP, IPTC, comments - since device type photos are served without a login. A device photo under 2000 px that carries none is stored as uploaded instead of re-encoded.

### Service level agreements

- **Agreements.** Governance → Monitoring → SLAs: an availability target over a month, quarter, year or a rolling 7, 30 or 90 days, inside service hours and outside holidays, provided for the tenant, some sites or locations, a contact or a name. **New agreement** is a three-step wizard: the agreement, its members, then the checks that count, pre-ticked from what the members already run.
- **Members** are devices, VMs, addresses, prefixes, circuits (on the addresses cabled to their ends, or a monitor address such as the carrier's far-end gateway) and switch stacks, measured on the master's primary address, in check groups that say which checks count. Devices can also join by selector: site, role, device type, platform, tag or name pattern. A redundancy group counts a pair as one unit, and units combine as *Average*, *Worst member* or *All must be up*.
- #257 #258 #259 #260 #261 #262 #263 #266 #270 #271 - **Figures** come from the status-change history, stored per period, recomputed every 15 minutes and frozen seven days after the period ends; counting rules are revisioned, so a closed period keeps the rules it ran under. Service hours count real seconds across a daylight-saving change, and month, quarter and year to date start at local midnight. Exclusions take time out with a required reason, and planned maintenance on a member's device or circuit can be left out.
- **Analysis.** An agreement's Overview computes any period or range live, per day or hour, sliced by check group, site, check type, redundancy group or member: availability with an hourly drill-down, the error budget, where the down time went, a weekday × hour heatmap, incident lengths, latency, a members-by-check matrix and a strip per member, with the last twelve periods and a **forecast** for the open one.
- #274 - **Alerts.** Breached, at risk, low coverage and latency alerts go to any notification channel once per period, and two **burn-rate alerts** (fast: 1 h and 5 min at 14.4x; slow: 6 h and 30 min at 6x, both editable) catch a sharp outage early, checked every minute. **Latency objectives** - *99% of ICMP probes within 20 ms* - get their own figure, budget and alert.
- #264 #265 - **Credits and reports.** Service credits price tiers, a fee and a currency into every period, behind a new *view credits* permission. Period reports download as PDF or CSV and are emailed when a period freezes or on demand; only people who see every member and may view credits can change the recipients, and the member list shows only members the viewer may see.
- **SLA and Availability columns** on device, VM, virtual chassis, IP address, prefix, circuit, site and cluster lists, and a provider's Circuits tab - the strictest agreement against its target, and availability over a window you pick (*68% measured* when part of it went unmeasured). An object's Monitoring tab lists its agreements with **Add to SLA**; the device selection bar adds many at once.
- **Holiday calendars** are edited on a twelve-month view: click days, mark fixed dates **Every year**, paste dates and ranges or open an .ics file, with Undo for an import.
- A viewer limited to some sites gets a partial figure over what they may see.

### Topology Diagram

- #164 - **Maps → Topology opens on the Diagram**: one card per device in its role's colour, a status or monitoring pill and **card lines** under the name (IP, loopback, serial, custom fields - set under Settings → Topology, per role, per view or per device). **Detailed** gives every cabled interface its own nub and cable, **Simple** one line per device pair with a `2x` count. Lines are **Straight**, **Elbow**, **Bendy** or **Cyclical**, for the view or one link, and **link labels** carry the subnet and each end's port and address. Wiring and Flat are folded into Detailed and Simple.
- **Photo** draws a device as its type's front photo with each cable on its port, or at the photo's edge. Captions carry the card lines, and gear that is not rack-mounted can be drawn at its photo's own size (**Topology photo size** on the device, its type or its role).
- **Switch stacks** stand packed in one frame with the chassis' name on a strip, cables leaving by the outer sides; *Unstack* draws them apart, and a hand-picked map takes a whole virtual chassis from the device list.
- **Bands** stack the map into titled layers by role or device type, merge and split, with side bands and their own cable sides; **notes** add text, cloud, globe or building markers; **zones** and bands take any colour from the preset grid. **New view** starts blank or from the map on screen, and devices are dragged in from a device list.
- #164 - **Exports**: PNG, SVG, PDF (A4, A3, Letter or Tabloid, with a title block) or an editable **draw.io** file, as shown or Simple or Detailed, drawn from the map's data for the whole map or the visible area, with **Print**. Hierarchy, Logical, Virtual topology, trace maps and a tunnel's map export the same way.
- **Saved views are documents.** Undo and redo (up to 100 steps), Ctrl/Cmd+S to save, a prompt before leaving unsaved edits, and a save over someone else's newer save is refused with **Save as…** or **Reload**. A star beside the Views select sets the view a bare /topology opens for the tenant, for tenant admins or holders of the new *set default* permission.
- **Hide one line** by right-click - a cable, bundle, LLDP neighbour or BGP session - with its own eye in the sidebar.
- Hierarchy, Logical, Virtual topology, a device's Map tab and cable, interface and tunnel trace maps draw the same cards; a trace that dead-ends carries an **Incomplete** badge.
- **Big maps stay usable**: layout runs in a web worker, only cards in view are mounted, uncabled devices pack into a grid, and a map too big to fit opens on its busiest device with a **Partial map** chip.
- **One Maps menu** lists Site map, Floor plans, Topology and Virtual topology, sharing one toolbar, **Objects** sidebar, **Display** menu and unsaved-changes dialog. Layout and **Levels…** moved under **Arrange ▸ Layout**.

### Racks, cabinets and capacity

- #248 - **The rack page** draws the rack beside its facts with a **2D | 3D** switch; 3D shows the rack with photo faceplates and coloured ports, with **Front**, **Rear** and **PNG**. *Render* and *Images* draw each device's ports live - cabled by speed, free, reserved, disabled - with ports in use (`38 / 48`), a cabled port opening its trace, and a **Far end** line in the port hover card. On the rear, a full-depth server shows its rear photo instead of hatching.
- #277 #303 #304 - **DIN-rail cabinets** are a new place to mount devices: a control cabinet's plate with TS 35, TS 15 or G 32 rails, with types, roles, statuses, tags, custom fields, documents, journal and change log, and a Cabinets tab on sites and locations. A device type gets its size in millimetres and the rail profiles it fits; the device form and the cabinet's **Arrange** place devices on rails, checked before saving. Calibrated photos draw at true size, the page has a **2D | 3D** switch, and a floor plan tile can stand for a cabinet.
- **Rack and cabinet drawings export** to PNG, SVG and PDF (A4, A3, Letter or Tabloid with a title block) with a Print entry, drawn from the data like the topology.
- **Display** on the rack and cabinet: Text, **Ports**, and on racks **Show** all, front- or rear-mounted devices. A disk, PSU or fan marker lists its statuses as pills and changes them by right-click, on the device page, the drawings and in 3D.
- #247 - **Floor plans colour racks** by **Space**, **Power**, **Ports**, **Panel ports**, **Rack role** or **Status** (Display → Color by), in 2D and in the 3D room, with a legend that goes into the PNG. Coloured by racks, the plan opens a sortable, filterable **rack table** under it; pointing at a row rings its rack. Monitoring keeps the outline.
- #247 - **A site's Capacity tab** adds its racks up floor plan by floor plan - racks, devices, space, power, ports and panel ports - with thumbnails coloured by the measure you pick and the racks on no floor plan listed apart.
- #247 - **One capacity scale** for racks everywhere: green to 80 %, amber above, red above 95 %. A rack with no primary feed falls back to its PDUs' inlet rating, taking two or more PDUs as an A/B pair. The racks list gains **Power**, **Ports** and **Panel ports** columns, and the rack page's Capacity card splits **Ports** from **Panel ports**.
- #307 - A site has a **Racks** tab, beside **Cabinets**.
- #247 - **Port counting** is one rule everywhere: physical interfaces and front ports, virtual interfaces only when **Count virtual interfaces** is on (Settings → Component details), rear ports never.

### MAC tracking

- #284 #290 - **Switch ports show the devices behind them.** SNMP reads a switch's MAC address table - Q-BRIDGE-MIB with VLANs, BRIDGE-MIB as the fallback, and per-VLAN tables (`community@vlan`, or `vlan-N` for SNMPv3) - keeps learned entries only and maps each to its real port. **Learned MACs** show per port on the SNMP tab and under Components → Interfaces, a stack's table listing only members you may view.
- #306 - **Uplinks** are told apart by an LLDP switch neighbour, a LAG, more learned MACs than *Uplink above*, or the interface's own **Uplink: Automatic / Always / Never**, in its form and in bulk edit. An interface gets a **MACs** tab.
- **Where is this MAC?** The MAC page shows its **Location** (switch, port, VLAN, since when), **IP** and **Name**, and **Observed** lists every port and ARP table that saw it. `/macs` gains a **Learned** tab, and a MAC pasted into search in any notation shows the port it was learned on.
- Each MAC keeps its first and last seen per port and VLAN, and stays as history for *Forget MACs unseen for* (30 days). **Refresh MACs** re-reads a switch's table in the background.
- #305 - A **MAC tracking** card on Settings → Monitoring and **Per-VLAN MAC tables** (Auto / Always / Off) on SNMP profiles.

### Monitoring

- **Monitoring history that outlives the raw results.** Hourly records per check (30 days) and daily ones for good: time in each state, incidents, latency percentiles, spikes against the check's baseline and a latency histogram. Each check gets its own page with availability, p50/p95/p99, baseline and spikes over 24 hours to a year.
- **Explore** groups checks by site, role, device type, platform, device, prefix, VRF, check or kind, worst first; **Latency** lists the checks furthest from normal. The Checks list gains 7-day availability, p95 and baseline columns, and latency charts draw one check kind at a time.
- **Exclude an address from monitoring.** A switch on the IP's Monitoring tab parks every check on it - its own and inherited, on the core, Outposts and Zabbix - closes its alerts and leaves it out of every count and SLA, with an **Excluded** pill and facet. SNMP polling, Redfish, watched endpoints and discovery carry on.
- **Reset availability** for an address reused by a new host, from now or a date, with a required reason: figures count from then, the history is kept and marked not counted, and the tab says who reset it and when. API: `POST /api/monitoring/ips/<id>/exclude/` and `/reset-availability/`.
- Settings → **Monitoring** moves to **Devices & polling**, beside SNMP profiles and sensors.

### Maps

- #246 - **Link speeds on the site map.** Circuits, tunnels and cables between sites carry their speed - a circuit's commit rate, else its port speeds, else the cabled interfaces; a tunnel's own **Capacity**; a cable's slower end, followed through patch panels - as a label on the line (`10G`, `100/20M`, `4×10G`) and in its popover and inspector with provider, circuit ID and the ports at each end. **Display → Color by** colours lines by Type, Status or Speed, with a matching legend. API: `?include=capacity` on the line endpoints.
- #250 - The site map refreshes after a site or region is created, edited, moved or deleted.
- **Space map:** a block with child prefixes draws them and zooms in on click, a free block offers *New child prefix here* and *Register an IP here*, IP ranges show as amber strips, rows past eight bits draw as strips, and **Aligned** draws each row under the blocks it splits. The zoom path is in the address.

### IPAM & DCIM

- #172 - **VLAN status**: Active, Reserved and Deprecated join the status catalog, Active the default for new VLANs, with a column, filter and bulk edit.
- #176 - **VLAN bulk edit** moves VLANs between groups (refused with the VIDs named when they don't fit), sets VRF and description, and keeps VRF, zone and status inside the user's sites under enhanced site separation.
- #177 - **Wi-Fi security modes**: WPA2, WPA3 and transition modes for Personal (WPA3-Personal is SAE) and Enterprise, Enhanced Open (OWE), GCMP-256 and a PMF field; combinations that don't fit the mode are refused.
- #217 - **Routing on virtual machines**: static routes and BGP, OSPF, IS-IS and EIGRP instances, with a Routing tab and the `routing` block in the VM's config render. VTEPs and LDP stay device-only.
- #182 #249 - **Import from library** on Module types and Rack types, as on Device types; rack-type files import as rack types.
- #183 - **Bulk marker colour and icon** on sites, regions and locations; the Locations list gains row selection.
- #251 #252 #253 #267 - **Bulk actions on more lists.** Bulk delete on circuits, providers, provider networks, circuit types, wireless LANs and groups, and virtual chassis, with a preview of what goes, what is released and what is kept. Virtual chassis bulk edit, removing several members at once, and MACs in bulk - remove, clear from interfaces or unpair from IPs, with a dry run.
- #244 - **Names with numbers sort as you count** - DIMM 2 before DIMM 10 - in lists, related lists, routing config, trees and facets.
- #244 - **Spec sheets read RAM in GB** whatever unit a BMC sync recorded, VM memory too, and mixed disks read `2 × 2 TB · 8 × 10 TB`.
- An interface's IPs tab shows the full IP table, and a port marked connected can be cabled from the cable dialog.

### Everyday interface

- #243 - **Every field is a column.** A table's Columns menu lists everything its rows carry - fields, related objects one step out (a device's **Region**, rack, platform, IPs, config template) and every custom field - hidden until ticked, sortable and exported. Drag to reorder and press **Save** to keep the layout.
- #269 - **Named dashboards** beside your own - each with a layout, time frame, refresh interval and scope - shared with the tenant or groups, with widgets for SLAs, availability by group, slowest against normal, coverage and open maintenance, and a **TV** mode that cycles dashboards on a wall display. A deleted home dashboard no longer opens from the menu.
- #176 #286 - **Selections** stay on their rows, drop rows a filter hides, and offer *Select all N*; more than 1000 rows go in batches with progress on the button (*Deleting… 2 / 3*), and a failed batch stops there with what is left still selected.
- Headers, detail tabs and row actions stay reachable on narrow windows, and wide tables scroll in their own frame.
- Detail pages show their figures in the Overview cards instead of a strip under the title.
- #184 - The colour picker's preset grid fits short screens.
- Charts: the hover follows the pointer, hours follow the 24-hour setting, and dashboard charts open the page behind them.

### Faster

- #241 - **Faster lists, contributed by @deku-m.** A site-scoped user's permissions load once per request (`/api/me/` from 178 to 25 queries), a site-scoped list of 960 addresses went from 3.7 s to 0.9 s, and the IP, interface, cable, VM, statuses and permission lists no longer query per row. Thank you!
- #254 #288 - The device list prefetches its secondary and OOB address, config templates, cabinet and DIN rail instead of joining them (a page of 10 in about 100 ms instead of 280 ms).
- #296 - Tags on every list load into plain lists instead of a query set per row: all 960 addresses in 0.5 s instead of 0.9 s, a page of devices about twice as fast.
- #297 - The site-separation setting is read once per request instead of on every permission check: a site-scoped journal page from 35 to 13 queries.
- #298 - The interface list fetches parents, LAGs and bridges for the rows on the page instead of joining them for every interface.
- #282 - A bulk delete's preview costs the same whatever the number of rows, and the delete about half as much per row.
- #299 - The dashboard reads statuses and address counts with their rows.
- #300 - One- and two-letter searches no longer scan the whole search index; folded text is stored with each entry.

### Fixed

- #280 - Bulk delete and bulk update answered 500 for ids that are not ids or a body that is not an object; they answer 400 with the reason.
- #273 #275 - Dashboards and monitoring filters answer 400 for ids that are not ids, and the topology API reads a huge depth as an unreadable one.
- A bulk delete reported every row the database removed along with the selection - one monitored IP read *Deleted 7000 IPs* - and logged each delete twice.
- #283 - LLDP links to a switch stack were drawn once per member.
- #292 - The API and spreadsheet imports refuse a status the catalog does not offer that object type, as the forms always did.
- #302 - Changing one SNMPv3 key on an SNMP profile or check template wiped the other; an edit keeps the keys it doesn't send, and `null` removes one. Saving an SNMP profile also keeps settings its form has no field for.
- #242 - Settings → Updates no longer shows two contradicting steps for the nginx backup location.
- nginx can read Django's static files again; since 0.16.12 the admin and browsable API came without styling (403 on `/static/`).
- A prefix's address list answered 500 for an address stored with a mask by a script.
- A patch panel's photo showed its front ports with the rear ports' state, and clicking one opened the cable dialog on the rear port.
- SNMP interface samples are pruned after three days; nothing pruned them before.
- The fast lane reconnects after a database restart.
- The alert list's silenced flag ignored silences scoped to a device, and a layout saved with **Set as new-user default** was ignored.
- Business hours on contacts and providers showed a clipped AM/PM under a 24-hour clock.
- A cable or status colour saved without its `#` painted nothing on the topology map.
- The Regions list's bulk bar offered Rename and Clone, which never worked there.
- `scripts/build-release.sh` builds on a host without clang.
